latest_release.name: v0.5.2
latest_release.body:
SolverQuip now survives a dropped connection to a Quip TestNet node. A node or proxy can close an idle websocket after a couple of minutes, and before this release the next chain read failed with a raw transport error. Reads now reconnect, check that the node still serves the same chain, and try again once.

### Behaviour changes

- Chain reads that hit a dropped connection reconnect and retry once. If the retry fails, they raise `QuipConnectionError`, as the receipt methods document, instead of a raw `JSONDecodeError`, `WebSocketException` or `OSError`.
- A connection lost while submitting raises `QuipSubmissionError`, saying the outcome is unknown, because the extrinsic may already be on chain. Before, it surfaced as a raw `JSONDecodeError` or `BrokenPipeError`.
- A genesis mismatch stops at once with `GenesisMismatch`, also when found on a reconnect or at a finality deadline. Before, it was retried as a plain connection error or reported as a finality stall.
- The `quip` extra now requires `substrate-interface>=1.8.0` (was `>=1.7.4`) and lists `websocket-client>=0.57.0,<2` directly. On 1.7.x every read after a drop raised `AttributeError`.

### Packages

| Registry | Packages |
| --- | --- |
| crates.io | [xqvm](https://crates.io/crates/xqvm/0.5.2) · [xqasm](https://crates.io/crates/xqasm/0.5.2) |
| PyPI | [xquad](https://pypi.org/project/xquad/0.5.2/) · [xqsa](https://pypi.org/project/xqsa/0.5.2/) · [xqcp](https://pypi.org/project/xqcp/0.5.2/) · [xqffi](https://pypi.org/project/xqffi/0.5.2/) |

```sh
pip install xquad==0.5.2
```

Documentation: [developers.quip.network/docs/xquad](https://developers.quip.network/docs/xquad/)

<details>
<summary>Full changelog (3 changes)</summary>

### Fixed

- **xqsa**: Keep a genesis mismatch's type and raise the client floor
- **xqsa**: Report a connection lost during a submit as a submit failure
- **xqsa**: Retry chain reads over a dropped connection

</details>
